sweep_summary: Single works with stress in the title for Vafsi (vafs1240; catalog = set by morphology from Stilo's handout Table One): Bögel, Yousefi & Mirdehghan 2018 (LFG'18, open PDF at CSLI/Stanford) was already held by the project from the 9/16 download and was re-read in full. It is squarely about stress in this language but only at the verbal-complex and clause level: stressed punctual bǽ-, negative nǽ- and preverbs, unstressed durative ær-, stress shift onto a following vowel when æ elides (b-ím-diæ), oblique clitic =om vs stressed full form ím, lexical stress encoded in p-form (Table 6), and unmarked sentence accent on the pre-verbal element (pp. 93-98, 103). This REFINES the catalog's morphological coding (independent, partly acoustic corroboration for morpheme-conditioned stress in verbs, complementing the affix-conditioned nominal facts) but is SILENT on the default word-stress position for nouns, so the catalog's deciding source stands; the 2018 paper is a better the secondary-stress rule citation than the 2021 DOAJ abstract already used by the second reader (same analysis, full English text, open access). Nothing new needs acquiring from this item. Side attempts: Bögel's publications page lists no other Vafsi work beyond the 2019 Konstanz slides (held by the project, same facts); the Yousefi-Mirdehghan-Bögel 2021 Zaban Pazhuhi PDF/landing page (jlr.alzahra.ac.ir) was could not be reached by automated download (automated download 000, direct download failed); written at

new_statements.quote: From the above discussion on the unstressed durative marker, the stressed punctual marker, and the stressed negative marker, it becomes clear why the clitics assume their full form in (9), (8), (10b), and (11): with the durative marker, they have to remain in situ in the initial position of a prosodic phrase, because an adequate host is not available; with the punctual and the negative marker, prosodic inversion is possible, but the stress shift from the markers to the clitic again forces the clitic to assume its full form. Finally, with the preverbs, the clitics undergo prosodic inversion, but are not subjected to a stress shift and can thus retain their clitic form.
new_statements.citation: Bögel, Tina, Saeed Reza Yousefi & Mahinnaz Mirdehghan. 2018. Vafsi oblique pronouns: Stress-related placement patterns. Proceedings of the LFG'18 Conference, 88-108. CSLI Publications.

new_statements.reading: Within the Vafsi verbal complex, stress is a property of particular morphemes rather than of a positional count: punctual bǽ-, negative nǽ- and the preverbs are inherently stressed, the durative marker is inherently unstressed, and bǽ-/nǽ- hand their stress to a following vowel-initial element when their æ elides (b-ím-diæ 'I saw'). This is morpheme-conditioned (morphological) stress at the word level, with sentence-level pitch accent handled separately (unmarked: on the element before the verb). The statement is first-hand in the sense that a native-speaker co-author confirmed the data and the paper shows its own pitch tracks, but the descriptive generalizations are credited to Stilo (2004b, 2010). It gives no default position for stress in uninflected nouns, so it does not settle the catalog's open question (expected stem-final default).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Within the verbal complex, stress belongs to particular morphemes rather than to a syllable count: the punctual marker bǽ- and the negative marker nǽ- are inherently stressed, the durative marker ær- is unstressed, and when no stressed particle precedes, stress sits on the main verb (ær-góæ). A stranded oblique clitic lands after the first stressed element of the verbal complex and takes over its stress when bǽ- reduces to b- before a vowel (b-ím-diæ 'I saw'), so the clitic has a stressed form ím and an unstressed form om. Nothing in the abstract gives a default stress position for uninflected nouns.
new_statements.exceptions: The 'affixal form' of the oblique clitic in Stilo's classification is reanalysed as the clitic carrying stress (ím) when left without a prosodic host; the negative marker cannot co-occur with the punctual marker. No other exceptions in the abstract.
new_statements.identity_note: The 2021 abstract says the data are from middle-aged and older male speakers of Chehreghan and Vafs (Markazi province), i.e. the Vafs/Chehreghan variety, the same one Stilo (2004, 2010) and the 2018 paper describe.

new_statements.translation: [p. 75] The durative aspect prefix /æt-/ (ex. 10, where it surfaces as /ær-/) is unstressed and is therefore not a suitable host for the oblique (set-2) clitic. [...] The non-durative (punctual) aspect prefix /bǽ-/, unlike the durative prefix, is stressed. [...] 16. (a) prosodic inversion: =om bǽ-diæ -> bǽ=om-diæ; (b) stress shift: b-ím-diæ 'I saw'. [p. 73] The position of stress in the sentence in Vafsi, as in many languages, depends on information-structure constraints; nevertheless, in unmarked sentences the main stress mostly falls on the element before the verb.

new_statements.relation_note: Full Persian text now read: it restates, with the LFG p-structure formalism, exactly the morpheme-conditioned stress facts already held by the project from Bögel, Yousefi & Mirdehghan 2018 (stressed bǽ-/nǽ-/preverbs, unstressed durative, stress shift to the clitic ím, sentence stress on the pre-verbal element), all credited to Stilo 2004b/2010; it confirms the catalog's 'morphological' coding and the earlier abstract-only reading, and like the 2018 paper gives no default stress position for nouns, so the catalog's empty rule field stays open.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Inside the Vafsi verbal complex stress is a lexical property of particular prefixes: punctual bǽ-, negative nǽ- and the preverbs há(r)-, dǽ(r)-, ó(r)- are stressed, the durative æt-/ær- is unstressed; oblique person clitics are prosodically deficient and need a stressed host to their left, so after a stressed prefix they undergo prosodic inversion (=om bǽ-diæ > bǽ=om-diæ) and, when bǽ-/nǽ- lose their æ before the vowel-initial clitic, the prefix's stress shifts onto the clitic (b-ím-diæ 'I saw'); with unstressed ær- or phrase-initially the clitic instead surfaces in its full stressed form (ìm-ær-góæ). Sentence stress in unmarked clauses falls on the element immediately before the verb; in subordinate clauses usually on the initial complementizer (not on semantically empty ke). Lexical stress is entered per lexical item in the p-structure (LEX_STRESS); no default rule for stress position in nouns or uninflected words is stated.
new_statements.secondary_stress: none discussed (grave accents in cited forms such as kær-òm, ìm-ær-góæ reproduce Stilo's transcription and are not analysed)
new_statements.exceptions: complementizer /ke/ does not take sentence stress (semantically empty, after Stilo 2004b p. 21); the emphatic enclitic =(j)a is always stressed although clitics are otherwise unstressed (p. 65); the clitic cannot follow durative ær- because it is unstressed; 'sustained intonation' (لحن کشیده) phrase boundaries after coordinators -o/ya and after subjects block inversion (pp. 73-74, Table 4).
new_statements.identity_note: Vafsi (Tati group, NW Iranian), spoken in Vafs, Chehreqan, Gurchan and Farak, Markazi province, Iran; data from Stilo's corpus (Stilo 2004b Vafsi Folk Tales, Gurchani dialect; Stilo 2010) plus productions checked with native speakers by the first author.

sources.quote: The durative marker is unstressed and is therefore unsuitable to function as a host for stranded oblique clitics [p. 95] ... However, in contrast to the durative marker, the punctual marker carries stress. Furthermore, if the element following the punctual marker starts with a vowel, the punctual marker's æ-vowel is dropped and stress shifts to the adjacent vowel: (16) bǽ- (PUNCT) + -av ('come') + -e (3S.DIR) → báwe ('s/he came') (Stilo, 2004b, 15) [p. 96] ... The preverbs are all stressed, i.e., they are suitable hosts for a clitic undergoing prosodic inversion. [p. 98]
